items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: But you never got the notion to switch to the guitar and play Carl Perkins or Elvis Presley songs?

ctx.x: Some of the pop stuff, not very much jazz. I was trying to think of a guy’s name on the way over. I used to listen to him on WNEW every night while I did my homework. And he had a show where he played all kinds of jazz: progressive and big band and some Dixieland. Purple Grotto was the name of the show. Anyway, what was on just the regular pop radio were things like Eartha Kitt, you know, and oh Teresa Brewer, and like I can’t remember, but a lot of the popular songs that had nothing to with jazz. You know it was…
But you never got the notion to switch to the guitar and play Carl Perkins or Elvis Presley songs?

No. No. Never. In fact I didn’t consider a lot of that music, although Elvis did sing some of these love songs that were popular at one time. He added his own peculiar twist to it. And I thought that was peculiar. Anyway. Let’s see what else was I going to say. Oh yes, in terms of what was going on in the music world as we progressed through college. I was going over to a concert in 19 — I think it was the spring of ’58, maybe the fall, anyway, at Chi Psi they had a stage set up and a band from Syracuse called…
